## Problem

## Requirements

Given an array, determine the fewest swaps needed to arrange it in sorted order. Each operation may exchange the values at any two indices. The interview variants include:

- Sorting in **ascending** order, from smallest to largest.
- Sorting in **descending** order, from largest to smallest.
- Handling arrays that contain **duplicate** values.

## Examples

Descending variant:

```text
[3, 4, 1, 2] -> [4, 3, 1, 2] -> [4, 3, 2, 1]
```

```trueviz
{"v":1,"kind":"example","title":"Minimum Swaps to Sort (Descending)","input":{"nums":"[3, 4, 1, 2]","order":"desc"},"steps":[{"say":"Given array [3, 4, 1, 2] and we need to sort it in descending order.","panels":[{"type":"array","id":"arr","label":"nums","values":["3","4","1","2"]}]},{"say":"To sort descending, target is [4, 3, 2, 1]. 4 should come before 3, so swap them.","panels":[{"type":"array","id":"arr","label":"nums","values":["3","4","1","2"],"marks":{"read":[0,1]}}]},{"say":"After first swap, array becomes [4, 3, 1, 2].","panels":[{"type":"array","id":"arr","label":"nums","values":["4","3","1","2"],"marks":{"write":[0,1]}}]},{"say":"Now 1 and 2 are out of order for descending; 2 should come before 1, so swap them.","panels":[{"type":"array","id":"arr","label":"nums","values":["4","3","1","2"],"marks":{"read":[2,3]}}]},{"say":"After second swap, array is [4, 3, 2, 1], which is sorted descending. Total swaps = 2.","panels":[{"type":"array","id":"arr","label":"nums","values":["4","3","2","1"],"marks":{"found":[0,1,2,3]}}]}],"expected":"2"}
```



The minimum is 2 swaps.

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

Think of the array as a permutation and decompose it into cycles of elements that need to be rearranged.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

For a cycle of length L, the minimum swaps needed is L-1, because each swap can place at least one element correctly.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3</summary>

Sum over all cycles: total swaps = sum (cycle_length - 1) = n - number_of_cycles.

</details>
